content.text:
You can pay federal taxes online through the IRS:

**Best option for most individuals:** **IRS Direct Pay** — pay from a checking or savings account for free, no sign-in required. It can be used for balance due, estimated tax, extension payments, amended return payments, and payment plans. ([irs.gov](https://www.irs.gov/payments/direct-pay?utm_source=openai))

**Start here:** Go to the IRS **Payments** page and choose:
- **Direct Pay with bank account** — free
- **Debit/credit card or digital wallet** — processing fees apply
- **IRS Online Account** — view balance/payment history and pay
- **EFTPS** — mainly for businesses or large/recurring federal tax payments ([irs.gov](https://www.irs.gov/payments?utm_source=openai))

A few notes:
- Direct Pay gives you a **confirmation number**—save it.
- You can generally **change or cancel** a scheduled Direct Pay payment up to 2 days before the payment date. ([irs.gov](https://www.irs.gov/payments/pay-personal-taxes-from-your-bank-account?utm_source=openai))
- If you’re paying business payroll/federal tax deposits, use **EFTPS** or the IRS business payment options; card payments are not for employers’ federal tax deposits. ([irs.gov](https://www.irs.gov/payments/eftps-the-electronic-federal-tax-payment-system?utm_source=openai))

To avoid scams, type **IRS.gov/payments** directly into your browser rather than clicking ads or unofficial links.
